official.deadline_central_display: Applications accepted continuously 1 May - 1 February; consideration dates 1 August, 1 November and 1 February
official.deadline_note: Applications are accepted continuously from 1 May through 1 February, with consideration dates of 1 August, 1 November and 1 February. The next consideration date is 1 November 2026; the cycle then closes on 1 February 2027 and applications for the following year open on 1 May.
official.application_cycle: Applications for the 2026-27 academic year opened 1 May 2026; the cycle closes 1 February 2027
official.status_note: The Indspire programme page states that applications are accepted continuously from 1 May through 1 February with consideration dates of 1 August, 1 November and 1 February, and the FAQ states the application remains active from September 2026 to August 2027, carrying forward until the cycle closes on 1 February 2027.
benefits: Funds are awarded to the student to use as they wish - tuition, childcare, food, cultural support, shelter, travel, and much more.
In 2026 Indspire awarded over 9,500 applications totalling 33,336,500 CAD.
Since 1996 Indspire has awarded 313,535,200 CAD to Indigenous students.
Certain awards must be applied directly to a student's academic account; in those cases the student is notified if the award will be transferred to their educational institution.
All awards are disbursed by electronic funds transfer directly to the student's personal bank account.
eligibility: Registered First Nations (Status or non-Status), Metis or Inuit.
Enrolled in an accredited university, college, skilled-trades program, secondary school or doctoral and post-doctoral program, anywhere in Canada.
Must show financial need; all students are required to demonstrate financial need, though Indspire also offers a very limited number of scholarships that are not based on financial need.
Part-time study is possible: the application is intended for students meeting a minimum course-load requirement of 60%, or 40% with a disability-related accommodation, and exceptions are limited.
Studying outside Canada is possible only for students enrolled in a graduate-level program.
Students enrolled in a fellowship or residency program are not eligible.
requirements: Complete only one application per academic year; you must log in, review your draft, update your information and documents and submit it for the new academic year.
Indigenous registration must be documented with a photocopy of the front and back of a valid Status Card, Metis card or Inuit Enrolment card in accordance with Indspire's policy.
Proof of enrolment must confirm full-time or part-time enrolment for the Fall 2026 / Winter 2027 academic year.
Grades must include final marks from the most recent, completed academic year or program.
Every document must contain the student's name, the school's name and the academic term or terms.
Community participation is scored; volunteering from any setting counts, including classroom monitors, study groups, coaching, charity fundraisers, student council and ceremony participation.
documents: Photocopy of the front and back of a valid Status Card, Metis card or Inuit Enrolment card as proof of Indigenous registration.
Official proof of enrolment - a letter from the Registrar's Office or a class schedule clearly showing the student's name, the school's name and the applicable school term.
Grades with final marks from the most recent, completed academic year or program.
selection_criteria: Financial need, merit and community participation decide awards and bursaries; scholarships are assessed on merit alone.
Amounts vary based on several factors, including the assessed financial need of applicants, the number of applicants, fields of study and the availability of funds.
Monthly living expenses are calculated automatically using standard monthly living costs based on Canada Student Loans, derived from the applicant's province, family status and number of dependents.
coverage: Unrestricted funds that the student can use as they wish: tuition, childcare, food, cultural support, shelter, travel and more.
Indspire awarded 33,336,500 CAD to more than 9,500 applications in 2026.
Living costs are calculated into the assessed financial need using Canada Student Loan standard monthly living costs by province, family status and dependents.
application_method: Submit only one application per academic year; the application opens on 1 May and remains active until the cycle closes on 1 February 2027.
Upload the three required documents: proof of Indigenous registration, proof of enrolment and grades.
Allow Indspire to calculate monthly living expenses from your province, family status and dependents.
If not awarded at the first consideration date, the application is automatically carried forward and considered at subsequent dates until the cycle closes.
official.application_route: One online application per academic year through the Indspire site, with the three required documents uploaded; a single application enters you for all available bursaries, scholarships and awards.
official.study_mode: Full-time or part-time is accepted: the minimum course-load requirement is 60%, or 40% with a disability-related accommodation, and exceptions are limited.
official.citizenship_residency: No Canadian citizenship requirement is published; enrolees at accredited institutions anywhere in Canada are eligible, and graduate-level study outside Canada is possible.
official.international_eligibility: Studying outside Canada is permitted only for students enrolled in a graduate-level programme.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Any accredited academic, skilled-trades or doctoral and post-doctoral programme; the skilled-trades stream covers certificate or diploma programs of one to four years. Students enrolled in a fellowship or residency programme are not eligible.
official.duration: Skilled-trades stream: certificate or diploma programmes of one to four years. For academic programmes the duration follows the student's enrolment; applications must be resubmitted each academic year.
official.description: On the strength of a conviction that education is the key to empowering Indigenous communities, Indspire is Canada's largest charity supporting Indigenous post-secondary students. Since 1996, through its Building Brighter Futures: Bursaries, Scholarships and Awards Program, it has awarded 313,535,200 CAD to more than 9,500 recipients, and in 2026 alone it awarded 33,336,500 CAD to more than 9,500 applications.

not_confirmed: funding_amount as a single value - Indspire states that amounts vary with assessed financial need, number of applicants, fields of study and availability of funds, so it publishes only programme totals of 33,336,500 CAD in 2026 and 313,535,200 CAD since 1996 rather than individual award values
funding_period - no per-award cadence is published; awards are tied to the program of study and academic year specified on the application form

tuition_coverage as an explicit statement - the page states funds may be used for tuition, childcare, food, cultural support, shelter, travel and more, so it is genuinely unrestricted rather than strictly a tuition scholarship
verification.notes: Indspire's Building Brighter Futures page and its programme FAQ were read in full on its own domain. The unrestricted use of funds, the requirement to demonstrate financial need, the three mandatory documents, the 1 May to 1 February window with 1 August, 1 November and 1 February consideration dates, the carry-forward until 1 February 2027 and the EFT disbursement and T4A treatment were all confirmed directly.

applicant_utility.summary: One application gets you considered for everything - bursaries, scholarships and awards - so there is nothing to gain from filing multiple times, and re-applying each academic year is mandatory. You must prove financial need, so an application from a well-off household will not be awarded, but the flip side is that the money is unrestricted: it can go to tuition, childcare, food, rent or travel, whichever is actually pressing for you. The three documents are all third-party - Status Card or Metis or Inuit Enrolment card, official enrolment proof and last year's final marks - and a fee statement or an acceptance letter will not be accepted as enrolment proof. Apply before 1 November 2026 to catch that consideration date.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Registered First Nations, Metis or Inuit students enrolled at accredited Canadian institutions, including skilled-trades programmes, who can demonstrate financial need and community participation.
application_readiness_checklist: Locate or request your Status Card, Metis card or Inuit Enrolment card well before you apply, since you need the front and back copied.

Request official proof of enrolment from your Registrar's Office - not a fee statement, acceptance letter or intent-to-enroll letter - and check every document shows your name, your school's name and the academic term or terms.
Pull your final marks from the most recent completed academic year or programme.
Check your course load: you need 60%, or 40% with a disability-related accommodation.
Log your community participation honestly, including school and community volunteering, since it is scored and a zero score lowers your chances.
Apply before the 1 November 2026 consideration date rather than waiting for the 1 February 2027 cycle close.
common_rejection_risks: Not demonstrating financial need - all students are required to show it, with only a very limited set of merit-only scholarships exempt.
Using a letter of acceptance as proof of enrolment, or a fee statement, intent-to-enrol letter or student contract.
Documents missing the school name, the academic term or terms, or the student's name.
Enrolment in a fellowship or residency programme, which is not eligible.
Studying outside Canada at a non-graduate level.
A course load below 60%, or below 40% without a disability-related accommodation.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Indspire does not publish a maximum award value, and the award is calculated to assessed financial need, so you cannot assume the full cost of attendance is covered. Because the funds are unrestricted, treat the award as a contribution to your overall budget rather than a full-fee scholarship.
document_audit: Enrolment proof must come from the Registrar's Office or be a class schedule showing your name, the school and the term; acceptance letters, fee statements, intent-to-enrol letters and student contracts are all rejected.
If your official enrolment documentation is not yet available, an acceptance letter may be held as a placeholder, but the application is not complete until active course registration is documented.
All three documents must contain your name, the school's name and the academic term or terms.
If you did not sit a 2025-2026 academic year, you must supply final marks from your most recent completed programme instead.
alerts: Applications are accepted continuously from 1 May to 1 February, with consideration dates of 1 August, 1 November and 1 February - the earlier you apply, the more funding opportunities you are considered for.
Your application stays active for the whole academic year and is carried forward automatically until the cycle closes on 1 February 2027.
Only successful students are notified, so silence is not a rejection and you should keep the application current.

Awards cannot be deferred, must be applied to the programme of study and academic year on the application form, and are paid by EFT to your personal bank account within four to six weeks of your banking details.
Indspire issues a T4A because awards are treated as income, so plan for a tax slip.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You submit one online application per academic year with the three mandatory documents, Indspire calculates your assessed financial need and living expenses, the application is reviewed at 1 August, 1 November or 1 February consideration dates until the cycle closes on 1 February 2027, and successful students are notified at the end of the month with funds transferred by EFT within four to six weeks.
